scope: One new registry entry, EQ-015/H.54.v1, closing a confirmed gap: 'Reflective Dissonance' (the title term of 'When AI Expands Human Potential: Reflective Dissonance, Epistemic Agency, and Constraint', Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19215748) had zero Toledo presence anywhere despite an exhaustive full-registry text search. The paper's own abstract (verbatim, per a prior research harvest, glosa/knowledge/harvest_v0.3/aihp/kc-aihp-023.yaml, fetched live from the Zenodo API) states: 'AI expands human potential only when machine-mediated dissonance becomes disciplined revision under world-answerable conditions. This requires corrigibility, route-openness, criticizability, and domain-sensitive validation.' This entry formalizes only the FORM of that four-condition licensing conjunction, citing four already-registered Toledo objects (one per condition: EQ-015/S.09.v1 corrigibility, A.5/S.03.v1 route-openness, A.5/H.12.v1 criticizability, EQ-015/H.53.v1 domain-sensitive validation) rather than inventing new primitives for any of them, plus a relates-to link to EQ-015/E.11.v1 (the source paper's only other Toledo entry). Tiered Dr, not Definition/Th_coqc, matching the source's own narrative-thesis framing (not a stipulated definition, not a proved universal law) -- the accompanying Coq file compiles closed but proves only a narrow logical corollary (dropping any one of the four conjuncts breaks the licensing), not the real-world thesis itself, and the drift_note says so explicitly. Independently coqc-compiled in this session, re-verified after a comment cleanup: 'Closed under the global context' (axiom-free). Registry summary counts recomputed and cross-checked against a fresh group-by over canonical[] itself.
